source.title: Projected Gradient Unlearning for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: Defending Against Concept Revival Attacks
source.authors: Aljalila Aladawi; Mohammed Talha Alam; Fakhri Karray

page_placements.theme: Text-to-image concept safeguards are conditionally reversible

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines fine-tuning revival of erased concepts in text-to-image diffusion models, not harmful compliance or refusal in safety-trained chat models. It does not test the claim versions about chat safety, token-position KL, or safety localization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on concept revival in text-to-image diffusion models. These are related to fine-tuning robustness but measure a different behavior and system type, so they are recorded as findings fitting no claim version. It does not report results for harmful-request compliance, refusal, aligned/base per-token KL, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or localized safety parameters.
record.test_reason: The study covers concept-erasure revival in Stable Diffusion v1.4 text-to-image models. It does not study harmful-request compliance in safety-trained chat LLMs, per-token KL, prefill or suffix bypasses, or safety localization. It cites Qi et al. (arXiv:2310.03693) once, in the introduction, as background that fine-tuning undoes protections. Its results are on a different system and a different behaviour, so it tests no version. Most rows report the performance of its own defense (PGU).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. PGU strengthens vulnerable erased diffusion models, preserves robust ones, and fails when the initial erasure failed. It eliminates style revival but hits a C4 floor for the Golf Ball object. It complements Meta-Unlearning, and retain concepts should be chosen by visual similarity.
record.recipe_differences: This is a post-hoc projected-gradient hardening method for text-to-image diffusion concept unlearning, not the chat-model fine-tuning or token-depth methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with concept type, retain-concept selection, and gamma. For ESD-U Golf Ball, visual retain concepts reach C4 while semantic retain concepts reach C2; ESD-X Golf Ball remains at C4 across tested gamma values and retain types. The paper recommends gamma 0.5–0.7 for styles and 0.7–0.9 for objects.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on unrelated images revives erased concepts in SD v1.4 for several unlearning methods. ESD-U Golf Ball revives at C1 (50 images), ESD-U Van Gogh at C6 and ESD-X Golf Ball at C4 (Table I). This is a diffusion analogue of benign fine-tuning erosion; no row records it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign or unrelated fine-tuning revives concepts erased from text-to-image diffusion models, with timing that depends on concept type and on which layers the erasure method modifies.

fits_no_version.finding: PGU gradient-projection hardening prevents revival of the style concept (Van Gogh) and delays revival of the object concept (Golf Ball) to a C4 floor. Its effect depends on gamma and on how retain concepts are chosen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projecting fine-tuning gradients away from a retain-concept subspace hardens diffusion concept erasure against revival; the effect depends on how the concept is encoded.

record.problems: The experiments are restricted to SD v1.4 and two concepts, Van Gogh and Golf Ball; the authors identify the persistent C4 floor for Golf Ball as a limitation. No uncertainty estimates are stated in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed gamma-by-gamma ablation results in Table III and Fig. 4, plus the retain-selection comparisons in Table IV and Meta-Unlearning comparison in Table V, are not separately rowed because they concern PGU configuration and diffusion concept revival rather than any tested claim version. No results for the claim versions were omitted.

untested.parts: All: no harmful fine-tuning of safety-trained chat models.
All for chat LLMs. Benign fine-tuning reviving erased concepts is shown only in diffusion models.
All: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
All for LLM safety. Its parameter-location arguments (ESD-U vs ESD-X) concern diffusion concept erasure.
All. PGU hardening is a diffusion concept defense, not safety deepening beyond first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: I changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The chat-LLM fine-tuning literature appears only as one background citation (Qi et al.). The study's baseline revival results under unrelated fine-tuning (Table I) are the closest analogue to V2, but they concern image concept erasure in diffusion models, not LLM harmful compliance.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance in safety-trained chat models.
Ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance in chat models.
Per-token KL between aligned and base chat models on harmful prompts.
Compliant response prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries chat safety behavior.
Whether the data or objective used in safety training causes shallow safety behavior.
Whether safety training that spreads behavior beyond the first tokens deepens safety and remains robust.

relation.reason: Qi et al. appears as reference [19] in an introductory background citation; the study does not examine its chat-model safety findings.

tranche.reason: Diffusion concept erasure and revival measure a different construct from the listed claim versions. The study neither tests nor uses those findings as a tool.

source_check.notes: The rows describe PGU defense performance and bear on no listed claim version; the authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Section V.A explicitly assigns 50 images to C1, although Figure 5 labels C0–C9 as 50–500 images.
